**English** | [简体中文](#简体中文)

## LiteScriptManager v0.1.4

The updater stops depending on `api.github.com`. The REST API allows 60 calls an hour per address, and a shared connection regularly spends them, which left the update check unable to run at all — not "offline", just told to wait. The check now retries through the partner project's release-page scheme, which reads the tag and the installer's SHA-256 from plain `github.com` and costs no quota, and the download keeps the `releases/latest/download/<name>` URL as its last candidate. The settings page also stops letting a stale reply overwrite a newer answer. No database change, and existing settings, schedules, triggers and history carry over.

## New

### A second check path, with no API quota

`check` and the startup auto-check now go through `fetch_latest_with_fallback`: the REST API first, unchanged, then the release-page scheme on any failure.

- The version comes from the `releases/latest` redirect to `releases/tag/<tag>`; the installer name and its SHA-256 come from `SHA256SUMS.txt`. No API call is made on this path, so it works when the quota is spent.
- A release that has no update still returns on the first call — the checksum manifest is only fetched when there is something to install.
- Which path answered is written to the app log (a warning naming the primary failure, then a line confirming the fallback answered), so a fallback is visible instead of looking like the only path there ever was.
- When both fail, the error the UI shows is the fallback's; the primary's reason is in the log line above it. "GitHub is unreachable" and "this release has no checksum" no longer read the same, because they are different log lines rather than one generic failure.

### The download falls back too

`install_latest` already tried the asset's `browser_download_url` and then the API asset URL. It now appends `releases/latest/download/<name>` as a final candidate — the one URL that needs neither the API nor a tag. The allowlist, the size cap, the `MZ` check and the mandatory SHA-256 comparison are unchanged: a fallback that skipped verification would be worse than no fallback.

### The release publishes the manifest it needs

The release workflow now writes `SHA256SUMS.txt` next to the per-installer `<installer>.exe.sha256` files and uploads it. The per-installer file still serves the API path; the manifest is what the fallback reads. Both are written with LF endings and no BOM: the parser splits on `\n`, and a trailing `\r` would stick to the installer name.

## Fixes

### A stale reply could resurrect an old update result

The settings page restores the startup check's cached result with `last_update_result`, and a manual check that failed cleared the update info — after which the cached reply could land and put the old result back on screen, with an install button for a release the user had just failed to check. Cache restore is now skipped once a manual check has started.

The same reply could also write to a component that no longer exists: every in-flight `load`, `getVersion` and update reply now checks a `disposed` flag before touching state, so leaving the settings tab no longer produces dead state writes or a toast from a window that is gone.

## Upgrading

- `LiteScriptManager_0.1.4_x64-setup.exe` is the per-user NSIS installer; no administrator rights needed. Windows 10/11 (x64) with the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime.
- The database schema is unchanged; settings, schedules, triggers and run history are carried over from v0.1.3.
- The release carries `LiteScriptManager_0.1.4_x64-setup.exe`, its `.sha256`, and `SHA256SUMS.txt`. All three matter: the API path reads the first checksum, the fallback reads the manifest, and the updater still refuses to install without one.
- Machines that were stuck on the spent-API-quota error can now check again — that is the failure this release removes.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/Jaspersol/lite-script-manager/compare/v0.1.3...v0.1.4

## 简体中文

## LiteScriptManager v0.1.4

更新器不再依赖 `api.github.com`。REST API 每 IP 每小时只有 60 次配额，共享出口 IP 经常把它用完，于是「检查更新」干脆跑不起来——不是断网，是被要求等。现在检查失败后会再走 partner 项目的那套发布页方案：从普通 `github.com` 读出 tag 与安装包的 SHA-256，不消耗任何配额；下载也把 `releases/latest/download/<name>` 保留为最后一档候选。设置页也不再让一个过期的回包覆盖更新的结果。数据库结构没有变化，已有的设置、计划、触发器和历史记录都可直接沿用。

## 新增

### 第二条检查路径，不消耗 API 配额

`check` 与启动时的自动检查现在都走 `fetch_latest_with_fallback`：先走 REST API（原样不动），任何失败都切到发布页方案。

- 版本来自 `releases/latest` 到 `releases/tag/<tag>` 的重定向；安装包名与它的 SHA-256 来自 `SHA256SUMS.txt`。这条路径一次 API 都不调用，因此配额用尽时依然可用。
- 没有更新时第一次调用就返回——只有确实有东西可装时才去取校验清单。
- 实际走的是哪条路会写进应用日志（`检查更新主路径失败，切换备用方案: …`，然后是 `已通过备用方案完成检查更新`），于是兜底是看得见的，而不是假装本来就只有这一条路。
- 两条都失败时，界面返回的是兜底那条的错，主路径的原因在它上面那行日志里。「GitHub 连不上」和「这个发布没有校验文件」因此不再读起来像同一件事——它们是不同的日志行，而不是一句笼统的失败。

### 下载也跟着兜底

`install_latest` 原本依次试资产的 `browser_download_url` 与 API 资产地址，现在把 `releases/latest/download/<name>` 追加为最后一档候选——那是唯一既不需要 API、也不需要 tag 的地址。域名白名单、体积上限、`MZ` 校验与强制的 SHA-256 比对都没有变：一个跳过校验的兜底比没有兜底更糟。

### 发布里带上它需要的清单

Release 工作流现在会在逐个安装包的 `<安装包名>.exe.sha256` 旁边再写一份 `SHA256SUMS.txt` 并一起上传。前者仍供 API 路径使用，后者是兜底要读的清单。两者都写成 LF、无 BOM：解析按 `\n` 切分，行尾多一个 `\r` 会粘在安装包名后面。

## 修复

### 过期回包会把旧的更新结果重新翻出来

设置页靠 `last_update_result` 恢复启动检查的结果，而一次失败的手动检查会清空更新信息——随后那个缓存回包可能落地，把旧结果重新放到界面上，还带着一个「下载并安装」按钮，指向刚才明明检查失败的版本。现在只要手动检查已经开始，就跳过缓存恢复。

同一个回包还可能写向已经不存在的组件：所有在途的 `load`、`getVersion` 与更新回包现在都会先检查 `disposed` 标志，离开设置页不会再产生无效的状态写入，也不会从一个已经关掉的窗口弹出提示。

## 升级

- `LiteScriptManager_0.1.4_x64-setup.exe` 是按用户安装的 NSIS 安装包，无需管理员权限。要求 Windows 10/11（x64）以及 Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime。
- 数据库结构没有变化，设置、计划、触发器与历史记录都可从 v0.1.3 直接沿用。
- 本次发布包含 `LiteScriptManager_0.1.4_x64-setup.exe`、它的 `.sha256`，以及 `SHA256SUMS.txt`。三个都重要：API 路径读第一个校验文件，兜底读清单，而没有校验值的包更新器依然拒绝安装。
- 一直卡在「GitHub API 访问次数已用完」的机器现在可以再查一次了——这正是本版去掉的那种失败。

**完整变更：** https://github.com/Jaspersol/lite-script-manager/compare/v0.1.3...v0.1.4
